title: STE Safety Instructions
description: Governs how a document marks a risk, orders the command, and explains the consequence.

rules.name: Mark the risk level with the right word
rules.message: Check that this block uses the risk word that matches its actual risk level.

match.question: Does this block describe a risk of harm to a person, or only a risk of damage to data, systems, or equipment? Harm to a person takes the higher marker; damage alone takes the lower one; when both apply, use the higher marker.

examples.bad: CAUTION: This command deletes every snapshot and cannot be undone.
examples.good: WARNING: This command deletes every snapshot. You cannot recover the data.

examples.bad: This command deletes every snapshot and cannot be undone.
examples.good: WARNING: This command deletes every snapshot. You cannot recover the data.

rules.fix: Add the correct risk marker, or raise the existing marker to match the consequence.

citation.note: Two halves. Whether a marker is present is mechanizable (a destructive-command detector can require one) but classifying the severity requires knowing the real consequence, so the rule stays judgement. In software documentation the higher marker maps to unrecoverable data loss or a security exposure and the lower one to a recoverable failure; that mapping is our adaptation, since the specification's own split is injury against equipment damage. Enforced at every tier, and the category weight is raised, because a missing warning is the highest-cost defect in a runbook.

rules.name: Start a safety block with the command or the condition
rules.message: This safety block does not open with a command or condition ("{match}").

examples.bad: WARNING: There is a risk of data loss when you run this command with the force flag.
examples.good: WARNING: Do not use the force flag on a production database. The force flag deletes every row.

examples.bad: CAUTION: The cache can serve stale reads for one hour after you change the config.
examples.good: CAUTION: Wait one hour after you change the config. The cache serves stale reads until then.

rules.fix: Move the command or the condition to the first sentence of the block.

citation.note: The rule wants the actionable part first, because a reader who stops after one line must still know what to do. The pattern matches the failure (a marker followed by a descriptive opener) rather than trying to recognize every valid imperative. Tested: both bad examples match; both good examples do not; and "WARNING: Rotate the key before the audit" does not match. Issue 9 changed one adjective in this rule's wording relative to Issue 7 without changing its substance.
